[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Split Sort** [CF 1863B · Split Sort](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1863/B){rating="1100"}

Look at pairs of consecutive *values* $(v, v+1)$ and where they sit, $\text{pos}[v]$ and $\text{pos}[v+1]$. A split at $x$ is stable on each side, so it changes the relative order of $v$ and $v+1$ only when they fall on different sides, that is only when $x = v + 1$, and then it puts $v$ first. So every pair that starts out backwards ($\text{pos}[v+1] < \text{pos}[v]$) needs its own operation, and one operation per such pair suffices: the answer is the number of backwards pairs.

[Solved in full in @sec-part-p1-b.]{.card-link}

:::
